topIssues.title: op-node: reactive runtime config reload on unsafe block signer mismatch
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
## Problem

When the unsafe block signer address is rotated in the L1 `SystemConfig` contract, op-node verifier nodes experience a **stale signer window** during which they reject valid blocks from the new signer.

The unsafe block signer is loaded as a **runtime config** — it's explicitly excluded from derivation ([`system_config.go:142-144`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/80b646e794/op-node/rollup/derive/system_config.go#L142-L144)) and instead fetched by a **periodic background reload loop** ([`node.go:454-487`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/80b646e794/op-node/node/node.go#L454-L487)) that reads the value from L1 contract storage (`eth_getStorageAt`) at a configurable interval (default: **10 minutes**).

During gossip validation, the block signature is checked against the currently loaded signer address ([`gossip.go:445-463`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/80b646e794/op-node/p2p/gossip.go#L445-L463)). If the signer was rotated on L1 but the node hasn't reloaded yet, blocks signed by the **new legitimate signer are rejected**.

Worst-case activation delay: `VerifierConfDepth × L1 block time + reload interval` ≈ **~11 minutes** with defaults.

During this window:
- Blocks from the new (legitimate) signer are rejected
- Blocks from the old signer continue to be accepted
- The node falls behind on the unsafe chain until the reload fires

## Proposed Solution

Add a **reactive reload mechanism**: when a gossip block fails signature verification, trigger an early runtime config reload (rate-limited to prevent abuse).

### Design

1. **Reload channel**: Pass a `chan struct{}` into `BuildBlocksValidator` alongside the existing `GossipRuntimeConfig`. On signature mismatch, send a non-blocking signal on this channel.

2. **Rate limiting**: The reloader goroutine in `initRuntimeConfig` consumes from this channel but enforces a **minimum cooldown** (e.g., 2 seconds) between reactive reloads to prevent L1 RPC abuse from attacker-crafted invalid blocks.

3. **Confirmation depth**: Reactive reloads still apply `VerifierConfDepth` — the signer rotation should be timed so that the L1 update is confirmed before the sequencers switch over.

4. **Validation result**: Use `pubsub.ValidationIgnore` instead of `pubsub.ValidationReject` when triggering a reactive reload, so the peer is not penalized for a potentially legitimate signer rotation.

This reduces worst-case activation delay to `VerifierConfDepth × L1 block time + 2s cooldown`.

### Future improvement: per-peer grace window

A more nuanced approach would track per-peer invalid signature counts and allow each peer a small number (e.g., 3) of `ValidationIgnore` responses before escalating to `ValidationReject`. This would:

- Avoid penalizing honest peers during a signer rotation
- Still penalize peers that persistently send invalid signatures
- Reset the counter when the signer address changes (detected via `P2PSequencerAddress()`)

This could use an LRU cache of `peer.ID → count`, purged on signer change, similar to the existing `seenBlocks` pattern. This is left as a follow-up to keep the initial implementation simple.

But this may be more complex than necessary. Maybe we just put this behavior behind a `--expect-unsafe-signer-change` and only enable reactive runtime config reloading if this parameter is active, and only then use `ValidationIgnore` instead of `ValidationReject`.

🤖 *Generated by Claude Code and Seb (human)*

topIssues.title: flaky test: `TestExecutePayloadSuccess`
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
## Flaky Test

**Test:** `TestExecutePayloadSuccess`
**Package:** `rust/op-reth/tests/proofs/core`
**CI Job:** `op-reth-e2e-sysgo-tests`

## CI Runs

- https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/gh/ethereum-optimism/optimism/121652/workflows/c7a2af02-affc-4d0d-bd43-461f58d6a244/jobs/4731572
- Failed 2 times in a row with the same error

## Error

```
execute_payload_test.go:61: no state found for block number 1
```

## Context

The test sets up a system, funds an account (tx confirmed at block 1), then immediately queries op-reth for the state of block 1. op-reth doesn't have the state ready yet — likely a race condition between block production and state availability in the execution client.

Two other proof tests in the same package pass consistently (`TestL2MultipleTransactionsInDifferentBlocks`, `TestL2MultipleTransactionsInSingleBlock`).

Encountered while working on ethereum-optimism/optimism#19881.

🤖 *Generated by Claude Code*

topIssues.title: op-supernode: Superroot SLA Updates
topIssues.author: axelKingsley
topIssues.body:
The SLA of the Superroot object is ill-defined, but also it is not currently behaving as we'd like.

The addage from Proofs is "whenever you can get output roots for all the chains, you should be able to provide a super root"

What this means to me is that we should ensure two distinct categories:

1: the superroot should be eagerly available. That is, if there are output roots at the timestamp for all chains, let's construct the super-root

2: the extended information regarding verification and local derivation must accurately represent the condition of data which yielded the superroot. IE - if the root is built from un-verified components, that should be obvious when inspecting the verification and local safety information.


DoD: Super-Root API is fully integrated with Proofs testing.
Probably a co-task between @axelKingsley and @Inphi

topIssues.title: flaky test: `TestTruncateDatabaseOnELResync` — CrossSafe sync timeout during setup
topIssues.author: wwared
topIssues.body:
## Flaky Test

`TestTruncateDatabaseOnELResync` in `op-acceptance-tests/tests/safeheaddb_elsync/`

## CI Link

https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/ethereum-optimism/optimism/121646/workflows/ce5a39a0-34f4-49e2-ac4d-73dfad0b8596/jobs/4730402

## Error

```
operation failed permanently after 30 attempts: expected head to match: safe
```

Note: `"safe"` here is `types.CrossSafe` (which renders as `"safe"`), NOT `types.LocalSafe`.

## Error Trace

```
op-devstack/dsl/check.go:26
op-devstack/presets/singlechain_from_runtime.go:51
op-devstack/presets/singlechain_multinode.go:22
op-acceptance-tests/tests/safeheaddb_elsync/safeheaddb_test.go:15
op-acceptance-tests/tests/safeheaddb_elsync/safeheaddb_test.go:25
```

## Analysis

**This is NOT the same bug as #19661** (stale engine RPC address after restart). That issue was about a connection failure (`address unavailable`) during the stop/restart phase. This is a different failure with a different root cause.

### Where it fails

The failure occurs during **preset setup** — before the test's own stop/restart logic runs. At `singlechain_from_runtime.go:51`, the preset runs an initial sync check:

```go
dsl.CheckAll(t,
    preset.L2CLB.MatchedFn(preset.L2CL, types.CrossSafe, 30),   // ← "safe"
    preset.L2CLB.MatchedFn(preset.L2CL, types.LocalUnsafe, 30),
)
```

This waits up to 30 attempts × 2 seconds = 60 seconds for the verifier node (B) to sync its `CrossSafe` and `LocalUnsafe` heads with the sequencer node (A). The `CrossSafe` check is the one that times out.

### Why it may be flaky

Both nodes are configured with `sync.ELSync` mode and a `SafeDBPath` (lines 17-18 of `safeheaddb_test.go`). In EL Sync mode:

1. The EL syncs blocks via P2P (fast), advancing the unsafe head
2. But `CrossSafe` advancement requires the **derivation pipeline** to process L1 data and the **supervisor** to confirm cross-chain safety
3. If the derivation pipeline or supervisor is slow to start, or if L1 block production hasn't advanced enough, `CrossSafe` may not advance within the 60-second window
4. This is a timing issue that would be sensitive to CI resource contention

### Possible fix directions

- Increase the attempt count for the initial sync check when EL Sync mode is active (derivation/cross-safe promotion is expected to be slower)
- Add a more targeted wait for CrossSafe that accounts for EL Sync startup latency
- Check if the supervisor is slow to mark blocks as cross-safe during initial sync in EL Sync mode

topPRs.title: feat(nuts): add update-nuts and verify-nuts commands
topPRs.author: maurelian
topPRs.body:
## Summary

- Add `just update-nuts <fork>` — snapshots `current-upgrade-bundle.json` as a fork's NUT bundle and updates `fork_lock.toml` with the hash and commit
- Add `just verify-nuts <fork>` — verifies a fork's bundle hash matches the lock, then optionally checks provenance by regenerating from the recorded commit in a temporary worktree
- Extend `fork_lock.toml` schema with an optional `commit` field to track which commit produced each bundle

## Details

The `update-nuts` command is intentionally simple: it copies the existing bundle and locks it. Bundle generation (`just generate-nut-bundle`) is a separate step the caller runs first. This keeps the tools composable and avoids a hard dependency on `forge`.

The `verify-nuts` provenance check creates a detached worktree at the recorded commit, regenerates the bundle there, and compares byte-for-byte against the committed bundle. The worktree is cleaned up automatically.

Both scripts follow the same patterns as `check-nut-locks`: `opservice.FindMonorepoRoot()`, `BurntSushi/toml`, `crypto/sha256`.

## Test plan

- [ ] `just update-nuts karst` — copies bundle, updates lock with hash + commit
- [ ] `just check-nut-locks` — passes with new `commit` field in schema
- [ ] `just verify-nuts karst` — passes (hash matches lock)
- [ ] Manually edit the bundle → `just check-nut-locks` fails (hash mismatch)
- [ ] `just verify-nuts karst` after modifying a contract → fails (regenerated bundle differs)

topPRs.title: feat!(rust): update `reth` to `v2.0.0`
topPRs.author: jnoorchashm37
topPRs.body:
## Summary

- Switch the Rust workspace `reth-*` git dependencies from the previous commit pin to the released `v2.0.0` tag
- Keep the workspace aligned with the existing `alloy 1.8.2` / `revm 36.0.0` dependency set required by `reth 2.0.0`
- Include only the minimal compatibility fix required to build and test cleanly against the released `reth 2.0.0` APIs

### Key changes

- **`rust/Cargo.toml`**: replace the `reth-*` workspace dependency pins from `rev = "082c36e"` to `tag = "v2.0.0"`.
- **`rust/Cargo.lock`**: refresh the lockfile so the workspace resolves the released `reth 2.0.0` graph.
- **`op-reth` RPC compatibility**: add the required `GetBlockAccessList` helper impl so `OpEthApi` satisfies the released `reth 2.0.0` RPC trait surface.
- **Scope guard**: leave all repo-local package versions unchanged across `op-alloy`, `op-reth`, and `op-revm`.

## Test plan

- [x] `cd rust && cargo +1.94.0 check --workspace`
- [x] `cd rust && cargo +1.94.0 clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cd rust && cargo +1.94.0 test --doc --workspace --locked`
- [x] `cd rust && cargo +nightly-2026-02-20 fmt --all -- --check`
- [x] `cd rust && RUSTDOCFLAGS="--cfg docsrs -D warnings --show-type-layout --generate-link-to-definition -Zunstable-options" cargo +nightly-2026-02-20 doc --workspace --all-features --no-deps --document-private-items`
- [x] `cd rust && cargo +1.94.0 nextest run --workspace --all-features -E '!test(test_online)'`
- [x] `cd rust && cargo +1.94.0 deny --all-features check all`
- [x] documented `no_std` package checks for the Rust workspace crates affected by this dependency line

## Important note

The workspace already carried the `reth 2.0.0`-compatible `alloy` / `revm` versions; this PR moves the `reth-*` git dependencies onto the released `v2.0.0` tag and carries the small `op-reth` compatibility fix needed for the release API surface, without changing any repo-local crate versions.
